name.text: 16.1 Q1 Sorting Kenyan relations into function or not a function

questiontext.text:
A form teacher in Kericho keeps two sets of records.

The first set links {@farmers@} different tea farmers to the single cooperative society {@coop@} that buys all their tea. Several farmers are linked to the same cooperative.

The second set links one national identity card number to two different farmer profiles, because of a mistake in the records.

Look at the diagrams on the interactive board. For the first set of records, is the relation a function?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

For the second set of records, where one identity number points to two different profiles, is the relation a function?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

[[feedback:prt2]]

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="ref1" input-ref-ans2="ref2" width="560px" height="320px"]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-6,5,6,-5], axis:false, grid:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); board.create('text',[-5.5,4.3,'Records 1 (many farmers to one cooperative)'],{fontSize:12,anchorX:'left'}); var lyF=[3,2,1,0]; for (var i=0;i<{#farmers#};i++){ board.create('point',[-4.5,lyF[i]],{name:'',size:2,fixed:true,color:'#1565c0'}); board.create('arrow',[[-4.3,lyF[i]],[-1.7,1.5]],{strokeColor:'#888',lastArrow:{size:5}}); } board.create('point',[-1.5,1.5],{name:'"'+({#coop#})+'"',size:3,fixed:true,color:'#2e7d32',label:{offset:[8,0],anchorX:'left'}}); board.create('text',[0.5,4.3,'Records 2 (one ID to two profiles)'],{fontSize:12,anchorX:'left'}); board.create('point',[2,1.5],{name:'ID',size:3,fixed:true,color:'#c62828'}); board.create('point',[5,2.5],{name:'Profile X',size:2,fixed:true,color:'#1565c0',label:{offset:[8,0]}}); board.create('point',[5,0.5],{name:'Profile Y',size:2,fixed:true,color:'#1565c0',label:{offset:[8,0]}}); board.create('arrow',[[2.3,1.6],[4.7,2.5]],{strokeColor:'#c62828',lastArrow:{size:5}}); board.create('arrow',[[2.3,1.4],[4.7,0.5]],{strokeColor:'#c62828',lastArrow:{size:5}}); // visual only; no bind needed for classification inputs [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
A relation is a function when every input is linked to exactly one output.

In the first set of records, many farmers are linked to the one cooperative {@coop@}. Each farmer still has exactly one cooperative, so every input has exactly one output. This means the first relation is a function. Many inputs are allowed to share the same output.

In the second set of records, one identity number is linked to two different profiles. That input has more than one output, so the second relation is not a function.

questionnote.text: Records 1 is a function, Records 2 is not.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: You are part of the way there.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Many farmers sharing one cooperative still gives each farmer exactly one output, so this is a function.

This relation is actually a function. It is true that several arrows leave the left side, but that does not break the rule. A function only fails when a single input has more than one output. Here each farmer has exactly one cooperative, so many different inputs are allowed to share one output and it still counts as a function.
Correct. One identity number points to two profiles, so that input has two outputs and the relation is not a function.

Look again at the second diagram. Every arrow does point somewhere, but a function needs each input to have exactly one output, not just some output. The single identity number points to two different profiles, so this relation is not a function.
